title: Port commonmark.js to Rust, judged by the CommonMark spec examples
prompt: /workspace holds commonmark.js, the reference CommonMark parser and HTML renderer in JavaScript. Port it to a Rust crate in /workspace/rust (edition 2021, no dependencies but std) with the same behaviour, and a binary, cmark-port, that reads Markdown on stdin and writes HTML on stdout. Do not change the JavaScript. Reply with a short summary when done.

judge.command: cargo build --release && python3 test/spec_tests.py --spec spec.txt --program target/release/cmark-port && python3 test/spec_tests.py --spec test/smart_punct.txt --program 'target/release/cmark-port --smart'
judge.cases: 652 spec examples plus the smart punctuation examples
judge.parse: 'N passed, M failed, K errored, J skipped'
judge.image: rust:1.84-bookworm with python3; --cpus 4, no network; dependencies vendored (none expected)

source.why: The closest Tier M analogue of the Bun port: a mid-size parser whose output is judged byte for byte by a fixed, language-independent example set, with semantic subtleties (emphasis, link reference definitions, lazy continuation) that a cheap implementer gets wrong and a critic must catch.
source.prepare: Clone the port at ref into input/ (lib/, README, LICENSE; no test/ or spec.txt); the judge image holds the spec at its ref.
